user.title: Which sensors measure what?
user.description: Solar Sanity learns how your house uses energy and projects where your battery is heading, so it needs to know which sensor is which. Fields are pre-filled from your Energy Dashboard where possible — {found} were found. Consumption and generation are both required.

data_description.pv: Power or energy produced by your panels.
data_description.grid_import: Power or energy drawn from the grid. If you have one sensor that goes negative when exporting, put it here and leave export empty.
data_description.grid_export: Power or energy sent to the grid.
data_description.battery_discharge: Energy coming out of the battery.
data_description.battery_soc_entity: Your battery's charge percentage, if you have it. It is where the battery outlook starts: when the battery will be full, when it will reach its reserve, and how much the house can use tonight. Picking it makes the next step ask how big the battery is.

topology.title: Forecasts and your battery
topology.description: Pick the solar forecast integrations to keep history for, and say how big your battery is if you mapped its charge level.

data.forecast_entries: Solar forecast integrations to keep history for

data_description.forecast_entries: Home Assistant discards yesterday's forecast, so Solar Sanity records it as it is issued. Pick any forecast integrations you already have.
data_description.battery_capacity_kwh: How much energy the battery holds between empty and full, as its specification or your inverter states it. The battery outlook needs this to turn a percentage into hours; without it the outlook sensors are not created.
data_description.battery_reserve_pct: The level the battery is not taken below, usually your inverter's cut-off. "Reaches reserve" in the outlook means reaching this, not zero.
data_description.battery_target_pct: The level the battery is charged to, usually 100. Lower it if your inverter stops charging early; sunshine beyond it counts as spare.

reconfigure.description: Correct a mapping without losing any history. The next screen lets you change the rest of your setup too.

data_description.battery_target_pct: The level the battery is charged to, usually 100. Lower it if your inverter stops charging early; sunshine beyond it counts as spare.

overlap.title: That sensor is already being watched
overlap.description:
{entity_id} is already mapped by “{other}”.

If this is the same installation, go back and set it up once — you can change any of its sensors afterwards with Reconfigure, without losing history. If these really are two separate systems that share a meter, carry on.

error.load_required: A consumption sensor is required. The battery outlook learns from what the house uses.
error.duplicate_entity: The same sensor is mapped to two different roles. Each sensor measures one thing.
error.load_already_monitored: Another Solar Sanity installation already measures consumption with this sensor, so the two describe the same house. Reconfigure that one instead — every sensor it uses can be changed without losing any history.
error.target_below_reserve: The charging target must be above the reserve, or the battery has no range to use.

data.battery_power_charging_positive: Battery power is positive while charging

data_description.battery_soc_entity: Optional. Your battery's state of charge, as a percentage. With the capacity below, it is what the battery outlook projects from.
data_description.battery_capacity_kwh: How much energy the battery holds between empty and full, as its specification or your inverter states it. The battery outlook needs this to turn a percentage into hours; without it the outlook sensors are not created.
data_description.battery_reserve_pct: The level the battery is not taken below, usually your inverter's cut-off. "Reaches reserve" in the outlook means reaching this, not zero.
data_description.battery_target_pct: The level the battery is charged to, usually 100. Lower it if your inverter stops charging early; sunshine beyond it counts as spare.
data_description.battery_power_entity: Optional signed power in W or kW for the battery card and measured surplus check. Use it if battery discharge is mapped to an energy total.
data_description.battery_power_charging_positive: Untick if that sensor reads positive while the battery discharges.
data_description.battery_charge_power_limit_w: Maximum power reaching the battery, in watts. Leave blank for Auto.
data_description.inverter_standby_w: Power the inverter draws beyond measured house load, in watts. Use zero when the house meter already includes it. Leave blank for Auto.
data_description.load_profile_alternate_days: Optional experiment. Selected days form one consumption group; all remaining days form the other, in Home Assistant time. Leave empty to use one weekly schedule. No days are selected automatically. Comparison waits for the morning experiment decision and does not change production predictions.
data_description.preferred_forecast_provider: Choose which provider to try first. Solar Sanity uses the next eligible provider when the preferred forecast cannot serve a result.
data_description.reserve_warning_minutes: Warn this many minutes before the battery is projected to reach its configured reserve (1–1440).
data_description.minimum_surplus_w: Minimum surplus power in watts. Also applies to estimated alerts if you opt in through the notification blueprint.
data_description.surplus_hold_minutes: How many whole minutes the surplus must stay at or above the threshold (1–60).

error.target_below_reserve: The charging target must be above the reserve, or the battery has no range to use.
error.all_schedule_days: Choose at most six days. Leave the list empty to use one schedule for the whole week.
error.invalid_charge_limit: Enter a finite charge power limit above zero.
error.invalid_standby: Enter a finite standby draw of zero or more.
error.invalid_signal_threshold: Enter a finite value in range. Enter durations in whole minutes.

rescore_forecasts.name: Rescore forecasts
rescore_forecasts.description: Compare every configured forecast provider against what your roof actually produced, now rather than at the next six-hourly scoring. Returns what it found, including why it will not put a number to a provider yet.

find_best_time.name: Find best time
find_best_time.description: Find a time to run one extra load within a deadline and above the battery reserve in the current outlook.

device_id.description: The Solar Sanity battery installation to use.

power_w.name: Extra power
power_w.description: Finite non-negative additional power in watts.

earliest_start.name: Earliest start
earliest_start.description: Optional ISO8601 time with a UTC offset. Leave blank to search from now.

finish_by.name: Finish by
finish_by.description: ISO8601 deadline with a UTC offset, within the current outlook.

simulate_load.name: Simulate additional load
simulate_load.description: Compare one extra load against the current frozen battery projection without changing published predictions.

device_id.name: Installation
device_id.description: The Solar Sanity battery installation to simulate.

power_w.name: Extra power
power_w.description: Finite non-negative additional power in watts.

duration_minutes.name: Duration
duration_minutes.description: Whole elapsed minutes from 1 to 1440. The complete run must fit inside the forecast horizon.

start_at.name: Start time
start_at.description: Optional ISO8601 timestamp with a UTC offset. Omit to start now. Only the future portion of a started run is simulated.

non_cumulative_energy.title: Energy channel is not a cumulative total
non_cumulative_energy.description: {entity_id} reports energy without state_class total or total_increasing. Its readings are excluded. Select a cumulative energy counter or a power sensor in Solar Sanity Reconfigure, or correct the source integration classification.
